critical_code_review_comments: Backend reset endpoint is correctly idempotent (delete_one on non-existing session returns 200/ok). Good.

App.js L11 still hard-codes WS_URL='ws://localhost:8765' producing a benign websocket error on every cloud load (carryover from iter_4) — non-blocking.
Reset endpoint accepts an empty body and defaults session_id to 'default'; consider returning a 'deleted_count' alongside ok:true for observability (nice-to-have, not a bug).

context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_4's single failing flow is now green. Both root causes were addressed: (a) frontend processCommand recall regex was broadened to /qu['’ ]?est[- ]?ce que tu sais (sur|de) moi|que sais[- ]?tu (sur|de) moi|.../ so apostrophe-less variants are intercepted client-side; (b) on 'oublie tout' the frontend now POSTs /api/chat/reset {session_id} AND rotates sessionId.current to a new random id, so even if the user uses a brain query right after clearing, the server has no history and no memory is passed. Subtitle still passes through 'Vous : « ... »' while thinking — keep the wait_for_real_answer poll (~18s for Groq, ~5s for client-side branches). Stub window.open + speechSynthesis.speak.
rca of the issue: RCA from iter_4: post-clear recall referenced lasagnes because (1) apostrophe-less 'qu est-ce que tu sais sur moi' missed the strict regex and fell through to /api/chat, and (2) /api/chat replayed the per-session history (still containing the lasagnes fact) into Groq. Backend test test_full_lasagnes_reset_then_no_recall reproduces the same seed→reset→no-recall sequence at the API layer and passes (none of the 6 forbidden confident-claim phrases appear in the post-reset answer).
